source.title: The Origins of Stochasticity: Comprehensive Investigations on Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models
source.authors: Xiang-Jun Ou; Shuang Liang; Xin-Yu Hu; Rong-Hao Huang; Jing Wang; Shao-Qun Zhang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It compares downstream accuracy across model scales, bearing on V6, but does not measure pretraining loss or reproduce the original loss-scaling experiments.
record.gate_note: Section 3.4 reports accuracy and uncertainty against scale in Figure 5. The UQ-method comparison tables in Sections 3.2 and 3.3 do not test the claim versions and are not recorded as rows. Figure 5 gives no extractable numeric values in the text, so outcomes are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: Section 3.4 and Figure 5 compare downstream accuracy on TriviaQA, GSM8K and HumanEval across two sizes per family. This bears weakly on V6 in a new setting: an uncertainty-benchmark side analysis. The paper fits no predictive relation, uses only two scales per family, and does not measure pretraining loss, so it is not T1 or T2. The reader's T2 overstates it.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that larger models reach higher accuracy, which they call consistent with Kaplan et al., and give lower average uncertainty estimates, which they call an empirical scaling law of LLM uncertainty. They also assert that larger models are better calibrated, citing Abe et al., but do not measure calibration directly as a function of scale.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines output uncertainty and downstream accuracy across model scales, rather than fitting held-out pretraining-loss curves, forecasting larger runs, or testing compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that UQ effectiveness varies with task type and generation setting; the scale analysis is plotted separately for answer-only and reasoning-augmented generation.

fits_no_version.finding: Average output uncertainty (Semantic Entropy, EigV, NumSet, BSDetector) tends to be lower for larger models within a family, in both generation settings (Figure 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantified output uncertainty of LLMs declines with model scale.

record.problems: Figure 5 provides no numerical point values in the text, and the paper does not fit or quantify a predictive scaling relationship. The scale analysis uses accuracy and UQ scores, not held-out pretraining loss, training tokens, or compute.
record.rows_left_out: None of the findings bearing on tested V6 or the separate uncertainty-scaling result were omitted. Other reported UQ-method comparison results do not bear on the claim versions.

untested.parts: Predictability: no functional fit, no extrapolation, no link to pretraining loss. Only two scales per family, and the models differ in training data and recipe beyond size.

record.verdict_notes: The scale evidence is very thin. There are two sizes per family, the figure text is garbled with no extractable numbers, and the legend lists 8B and 14B scales absent from the configuration. Section 3.2's remark that UQ methods perform better on larger models concerns UQ effectiveness, not downstream accuracy, so it is not V6 evidence. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law fit against parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit or prediction of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute allocation experiment or parameter/token scaling with compute.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
No tests of power-law loss scaling in other modalities or training regimes.
The study reports accuracy against scale, but does not fit a predictive relationship, test extrapolation, or relate performance to pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitting choices, exponents, or departures from power-law curves.

rows.size_stated: Multiple scales; individual scale values not stated in the text for these plotted results
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream accuracy across model scales
rows.note: The authors describe larger-scale models as generally achieving higher predictive precision; the plotted points are not individually extracted.
rows.check: Accuracy is a property of model and dataset, not of the UQ method. The four A-*-R rows record one measurement four times and should be merged into one reasoning-augmented accuracy row. Evidence is qualitative and figure-only: larger circles sit further right. Only two sizes per family (Qwen3 1.7B/4B, Llama 3.2 1B/3B). DeepSeek-V3 is a single point of unstated scale.

relationships.condition: Qwen3 1.7B→4B and Llama 3.2 1B→3B on TriviaQA, GSM8K and HumanEval, answer-only and reasoning-augmented generation; qualitative reading of Figure 5.
relationships.reason: Authors state larger models usually achieve higher predictive precision (A-SE-R, A-SE-A and their duplicates). This shows only the direction of improvement, not predictability.
relationships.display_finding: Larger models usually achieve higher predictive precision, establishing improvement without quantifying its predictability.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
